name: Game Studio I
org: New York University Tisch School of Arts
summary: Helped first-year game-design graduates through code, game design, or visual art questions. Assisted professors in classroom management and facilitated peer feedback and playtesting.

name: New York City Hall of Science
summary: Ran a series of educational workshops and helped in the co-design of tabletop activities and games with their “Explainers”. We explored technologies for biosensing and real-time machine learning models for facial and emotion recognition from video streams.

bullets.text: Collaborated with Columbia’s ARNI lab for the brainstorming and design of these activities.
Helped in the organization of our annual Game Center Spring Showcase with more than 800 attendees. Specifically, I was part of the team involved in branding & printed materials.
Assisted in running a community-outreach event that allowed children, families, and adults to get hands-on experience with analogue game design by modding and creating their own games.
Assisted in running the initial playtest for a large-scale social game and artistic experience designed by Eric Zimmerman.
Led a 30+ member student club dedicated to neuroscience workshops, science outreach, and research.
Worked on biofeedback-based games and installations for events and hackathons for the student community.
Conducted research on motor rehabilitation treatments using a neuroprosthesis.
Co-developed software for the real-time data collection, recording, and preprocessing of a brain-to-brain synchrony study in education.
Co-wrote and published a review on the use of Wearable Devices in Education.
